# TerraScan: transferring a Sentinel-2 land-use classifier from Europe to India

*Technical report (step 8.11). Generated by `src/tech_report.py` from `results/`; every number below names its file.*

## Abstract

Land-use classifiers trained on EuroSAT reach about 98.52%-98.74% test accuracy on European Sentinel-2
images, consistent with the 98.57% reported by the dataset's authors. On 81 hand-labelled patches
from two held-out areas in Gujarat, India, the model picked for India (EfficientNet-B0) falls to 0.4486 ± 0.0071
(mean ± std, 3 seeds). Fine-tuning on 149 labelled Indian patches from three other areas raises this to
0.6831 ± 0.0311 (`results/india_after.json`). Further attempts to improve it (WorldCover-derived training squares, test-time augmentation and a seed ensemble, a frozen satellite foundation model) are reported with decision rules fixed before each
run: none beat the simple fine-tuned model. A change map of Ahmedabad 2018-2026 over-reports
change: 51% of 50 randomly checked changed squares held up. The full inference pipeline also runs in
a web browser and matches the Python pipeline on 272 of 272 squares.

## 1. Question

Does a model trained on European satellite images work on Indian land, and what does it take to make it work?

## 2. Data

- **EuroSAT** (Helber et al. [1]): 27,000 Sentinel-2 patches, 64 × 64 px, 10 classes, split 70/15/15 once
  (`data/splits/`). The RGB version for most models; the 13-band version for the band and foundation-model studies.
- **Indian patches**: Sentinel-2 Level-2A from Microsoft Planetary Computer, dry season 2025/26, five ~10 km areas in
  Gujarat, cut into the same 64 × 64 px patches. 368 were reviewed, 230 labelled, 138 skipped.
  Split **by area**: fine-tune areas (ahmedabad_city, narmada_bharuch, ankleshwar_industrial) and test areas (vadodara_outskirts, sanand_farmland).
- **Label tiers**: tier 1 = human-reviewed labels (the only ones used to evaluate); tier 2 = ESA WorldCover 2021 [4]
  mapped to our classes as *sets* (`results/noisy_labels_data.json`, agreement with tier 1 86% on
  155 squares; an agreement rate, not accuracy); tier 3 (pseudo-labels) was not used.
- **Pipeline details that mattered**: the +1000 offset of processing baseline ≥ 04.00 removed per scene from its
  metadata; per-colour linear calibration from Level-2A to EuroSAT's Level-1C colours fitted on European scenes only
  (`results/imagery_calibration.json`); median composites of all clear scenes of one tile, on one pixel grid.

## 3. Methods

- **Models** (EuroSAT): a small CNN from scratch, ResNet-18 and EfficientNet-B0 from ImageNet, ResNet-18 from
  Sentinel-2 self-supervised weights (torchgeo). One shared recipe; 3 seeds; every choice made on validation data.
- **Fine-tuning**: all layers, 10 epochs, learning rate 0.0001, 600 EuroSAT images mixed into every epoch so Europe is not
  forgotten; the last epoch is kept (no Indian validation set exists to choose one).
- **Validation on Indian land**: leave-one-area-out (LOAO) over the three fine-tune areas, 149 patches pooled. The test
  areas were scored in steps 4.3/4.4 and are not used for any later choice.
- **Decision rule** for every Phase 8 experiment: a change is kept only if its mean beats the reference by more than
  the two standard deviations added together; each rule was committed to git before its run.
- **Deployment**: ONNX export (largest logit gap to PyTorch 7.2e-06, `results/onnx_check.json`), a static
  website, and a browser port of the whole inference pipeline (STAC search, Cloud-Optimised GeoTIFF range reads,
  UTM projection, median composite, calibration, ONNX Runtime Web with WebGPU or WebAssembly in a Web Worker).

## 4. Results

### 4.1 EuroSAT (in distribution)

| small_cnn_v1 | 42 | 64×64 | 175,626 | 0.9615 (1 seed) | 0.9604 (1 seed) | 2.1 (1 seed) |
| small_cnn_v2 | 42, 43, 44 | 64×64 | 1,311,050 | 0.9874 ± 0.0007 | 0.9870 ± 0.0007 | 11.8 ± 0.1 |
| resnet18 | 42, 43, 44 | 128×128 | 11,181,642 | 0.9854 ± 0.0002 | 0.9849 ± 0.0003 | 14.5 ± 0.0 |
| efficientnet_b0 | 42, 43, 44 | 128×128 | 4,020,358 | 0.9869 ± 0.0013 | 0.9862 ± 0.0014 | 7.6 ± 0.1 |
| resnet18_sat | 42, 43, 44 | 128×128 | 11,181,642 | 0.9852 ± 0.0011 | 0.9848 ± 0.0011 | 14.3 ± 0.1 |

Consistent with published results (98.57% in [1]); not a claim to beat them.

### 4.2 Europe to India

Indian test areas (81 patches; also scored in steps 4.3/4.4): 0.4486 ± 0.0071 before fine-tuning,
0.6831 ± 0.0311 after (`results/india_after.json`). EuroSAT test accuracy goes from 0.9869 ± 0.0013 to 0.9828 ± 0.0006.

### 4.3 Attempts to improve Indian accuracy (LOAO, fine-tune areas only)

| Experiment | Result | Decision | File |
|---|---|---|---|
| Do 1,722 extra squares labelled from ESA WorldCover help? | hand labels only 0.655 ± 0.017; WorldCover only 0.438 ± 0.010; WorldCover then hand 0.575 ± 0.024 | No: coarse map labels made it worse. Hand labels only stay. | `results/noisy_labels.json` |
| Average each answer over 8 flips and turns? Over 3 seeds? | reference 0.655 ± 0.017; flips/turns 0.678 ± 0.029; seed ensemble 0.671 | Not kept: a small gain inside the seed-to-seed spread. | `results/india_ablation.json` |
| Does a frozen satellite foundation model (Prithvi-EO-2.0, 304M parameters) beat our fine-tuned CNN? | linear probe 0.570 ± 0.037 vs reference 0.655 ± 0.017 | Not better by the rule. | `results/foundation_models.json` |

### 4.4 Change in Ahmedabad, 2018 to 2026

50 randomly sampled "changed" squares were checked by eye on before/after pictures: 51% were real
change (95% range 37%-65%), so of the 319 reported, about 163 is real
(`results/change_check.json`).

### 4.5 Browser vs Python

8 box-years, one outside Gujarat: same scenes chosen every time: yes; same class for
272 of 272 squares; largest gap between square centres 0.0 m
(`results/browser_parity.json`).

## 5. Limitations

- Small tier-1 data: 230 labelled patches from five areas in one state, one season. Test results have wide
  ranges and the test areas were looked at twice (4.3, 4.4).
- 640 m squares hold mixed land use; one label per square is a simplification.
- EuroSAT's classes do not fit Indian land well (wide muddy rivers, residential vs industrial); see
  `results/error_audit.md`.
- Change maps over-report: about half of the flagged changes were not real in the checked sample.
- The multi-city evaluation (8.7/8.8) needs new human labels in other cities and was not done.

## 6. Reproducibility

Python 3.12 and pinned packages (`requirements.txt`); website in `web/` (`npm ci`). Every training script supports
`--fast-dev-run`; seeds 42/43/44. Each step's command is in the docstring of its script and in `configs/`. Checked
for this report: a fresh clone passes `pytest` and the website tests (checked from a fresh clone on 2026-11-26: all passed; tests needing the git-ignored data or model files skip themselves).
